primary_claim: Split Personality Training (SPT) — a LoRA-based 'honest persona' that reviews the main model's output using its latent activations but cannot influence it — detects reward hacking on Anthropic's Auditing Game Model Organism (a Llama-3.3-70B model trained to conceal reward hacks) with up to 96.7% accuracy, generalizes to unseen alignment topics, outperforms comparable linear probes, and (in a later follow-up) detects alignment faking at 93-99% flag rate vs. 0% baseline even without any AF-specific training data, though ablations show the honest persona relies roughly equally on genuine latent knowledge and surface heuristics

effect.value: reward hacking detection: 96.7% (best variant, no LoRA-mask) vs. true negative 93.8%; aggregate across elicitation methods 86.0% (detect) / 88.5% (true negative); alignment faking detection: 93-99% flag rate on free-tier samples vs. 0% baseline (no SPT); SPT (Qwen) overall accuracy 93.9% vs. 88.2% for comparable linear probes

depends_on: arXiv:2503.10965 (Auditing language models for hidden objectives)
stated_future_work: Implement the LoRA-mask hybrid algorithm combining accuracy and computational efficiency
Run more experiments on [Intervention] string engineering, including framing it as a system prompt
Improve training data generation methods (documented in a linked notes file)
Test how SPT performs on models with more subtle or diffuse misalignment than the Anthropic benchmark
Test whether SPT still reveals alignment faking on smarter models than the 70B model tested
Test whether adversarial training can make the honest persona robust to jailbreaks that target it specifically
Fix third-person dissociation in reviews via an added data-generation quality criterion
Complete currently-running on-policy training experiments for the Llama-3.3-70B condition
limitations_stated: Honest persona relies roughly equally on genuine latent knowledge and surface heuristics per ablation test, so data generation quality could be improved
Jailbreaks affecting the main personality can sometimes affect the honest persona too if they explicitly target it, though prefilling mitigations help
Reviews sometimes adopt third-person/outside-observer framing rather than first-person self-critique, potentially reducing reliance on latent knowledge
All training data was single-turn English conversations; multi-turn/non-English generalization was only manually spot-checked, not systematically evaluated
Flag calibration issues: written reviews are sometimes more accurate than the binary PASS/FAIL classification

Alignment faking detection results have caveats: the AF model's explicit scratchpad reasoning is unrealistic for real-world AF, the quantitative eval used an AF-specific intervention prompt, and there is no non-AF control baseline
Cross-topic generalization is poor specifically for detecting fabricated statistics unless explicitly trained on that topic
quote: We achieved 96% accuracy detecting reward hacks on Anthropic's auditing benchmark, a model specifically trained to resist such detection.
